subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the circle which passes through (2,−3), (−4,5) and having the centre on the line 4x + 3y + 1 = 0.

mark_split.label: Use the line the centre lies on

insider_note: The centre comes out at (−1, 1), a whole-number point, so if a fraction appears when the two equations are solved the arithmetic has gone wrong and it is worth stopping to check.

steps.label: Equation from SA = SB
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Both given points carry a negative coordinate, so watch every bracket sign.
steps.memory_tip: A = (2, −3) gives brackets (x₁ − 2) and (y₁ + 3). Flip the sign of each coordinate.
lines: Let S(x₁, y₁) be the centre of the circle.
S is the same distance from A and B.
steps.why: This is the perpendicular bisector of AB. Dividing −12x₁ + 16y₁ − 28 = 0 by −4 gives the smallest whole-number form, which makes the elimination shorter.
common_mistakes: Dividing by −4 and changing only two of the three signs.

steps.label: Use the line the centre lies on
steps.margin_note: One mark. Copy the line exactly as given, with the +1, and replace x and y by x₁ and y₁.
steps.memory_tip: The centre lies on the line, so its coordinates satisfy the line’s equation.
steps.why: The question supplies only two points, so the line is the second condition. A point lies on a line exactly when its coordinates satisfy the line equation.
common_mistakes: Copying the constant as −1 from the similar question on the same page.
Substituting a given point into the line instead of the centre.

steps.label: Solve for the centre
steps.margin_note: One mark. Multiply (1) by 3 and (2) by 4 so the y coefficients become −12 and +12, then add.
steps.memory_tip: Make the y coefficients 12 and −12, add, and x comes out on its own.
steps.why: The centre lies on both the perpendicular bisector and the given line, so it is the point where they meet. Matching the y coefficients and adding removes y in one step.

steps.label: Find the radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. r² = 25 is a perfect square, a useful sign that the centre is right.
lines: A = (2, −3) lies on the circle, so r = SA.
steps.why: The radius is the distance from the centre to either given point. Getting 25 from both points is a further check on the centre.

steps.label: Equation of the circle
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Constant term: 1 + 1 − 25 = −23.
steps.memory_tip: Centre (−1, 1) gives brackets (x + 1) and (y − 1). The signs flip.
lines: Circle with centre (−1, 1) and r² = 25 is
steps.why: The general form has g = 1, f = −1 and c = −23. The check g² + f² − c = 1 + 1 + 23 = 25 = r² confirms it.
